newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Gujral reshuffles portfolios of ministers.
newsitem.headline: India's Gujral reshuffles portfolios of ministers.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral reallocated the portfolios of some of his ministers on Monday and gave new jobs to women in his seven-week old cabinet.
The reshuffle by Gujral comes nine days after he inducted four women members into his council of ministers, taking its strength to 43.

As part of the reshuffle Gujral appointed Janeshwar Mishra as the new cabinet minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas, a portfolio he earlier held himself. Mishra was earlier in charge of Water Resources.

Gujral appointed Saleem Iqbal Sherwani, who was the Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, and Kamla Sinha one of the new women members, as junior External Affairs Ministers. Gujral continues to hold the External Affairs portfolio.
M. Arunachalam, who was the Labour Minister, is the new Chemicals and Fertiliser Minister.
M.P. Veerendra Kumar, who was junior Finance Minister, will be the new Minister of State for Labour with independent charge.
According to a government statement, Jayanthi Natarajan, another woman member, will be Minister of State for Civil Aviation and Parliamentary Affairs.
Ratnamala D. Savanoor will be Minister of State for Planning and Programme Implementation, while Renuka Chowdhury is Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare.
